text:
elaine_sales: Quick sync — Pacific Health (PH) wants a Private deployment POC in their AWS account. They need low-latency on-prem access and strict egress controls. Can we confirm recommended connectivity options and what we need for the network handoff?

sanjay_neteng: For low-latency onprem -> infra I'd propose: TGW + VPC attachments in PH account, and a cross-account Interface VPC Endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) from our infra VPC as fallback for restricted subnets. If they can open peering it's simpler, but they said security prefers endpoints.

kevin_se: +1. Important to clarify: do they want traffic hairpin through their NATs or direct to our ENIs? PrivateLink keeps traffic inside AWS and avoids IGW egress, which matches "no internet egress" ask.

mike_se: Also need to surface pricing options to procurement: estimate for Dedicated reserved (monthly commit) vs hosted with privatelink egress. PH asked if Private deployment still has metered egress costs on our side or if that's absorbed in Dedicated pricing.

elaine_sales: Procurement asked for a single-page network requirements checklist we can hand to their netops. Can someone paste the minimal port/flow list and the preferred AWS resources?

kevin_se: Minimal checklist (for PrivateLink-first POC):
- VPC: a staging VPC with /16 for the app (e.g., 10.10.0.0/16)
- Subnets: private subnets for workloads + endpoint subnets in each AZ
- Interface VPC Endpoint: com.amazonaws.vpce (redwood-private-endpoint) created in PH account
- Security Groups (endpoint): allow inbound TCP 443 from the PH workload SGs
- Route tables: no changes needed for interface endpoints (ENIs created in subnet)
- Egress: if any outbound to external services required, NAT through customer NAT GW (PH retains control)
- DNS: enable private DNS for the endpoint -> automatically resolves redwood hostname to endpoint IPs

Firewall/SG example snippets (give to netops):
- SG for PH app -> outbound rule: TCP 443 to VPC Endpoint SG (or CIDR of endpoint ENIs)
- Endpoint SG -> inbound TCP 443 from PH app SG
- Allow TCP 443 to 10.0.0.0/16 (our infra VPC) if they prefer explicit CIDR

Sample aws cli to create interface endpoint (for their infra team):
```
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id vpc-0abcd1234 --vpc-endpoint-type Interface --service-name com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-xxxx --subnet-ids subnet-aaa,subnet-bbb --security-group-ids sg-aaa
```

sanjay_neteng: Notes for TGW approach (if they prefer peering style):
- Create TGW in PH account, attach PH app VPC + our infra account VPC via attachments
- Configure route tables to send traffic to the attachment for the redwood subnets
- Make sure Transit Gateway route propagation and sharing work across accounts (RAM)
- Requires more org-level coordination but gives predictable latency and L3 routing

tamara_ps: Security asks: PH' security team will want answers in the questionnaire:
- Data classification (PH: PHI/PII) -> we need to confirm whether any model logging will persist customer data, and the retention settings for audit logs.
- KMS integration for keys -> PH requires CMK in their account vs ours? We should offer a pattern: customer-managed CMK for private deployments or HSM in Private.
- SOC2 / ISO attestations (we have these; attach links).
- Network segmentation diagram (they asked for a simple diagram).

elaine_sales: I have the sec questionnaire PDF. I'll upload to the thread once I get edits. Also they want the POC timeline (2-week window). Can infra accommodate spinup + tests in 10 business days?

mike_se: For Dedicated/private, timeline: 3-5 business to provision infra once we have VPC & endpoint permissions and their CIDRs. If they need custom kernel/quantization testing, +3 days. We can commit to a 10 business day end-to-end POC with clear cutover/demo dates.

kevin_se: Action items for handoff:
1) PH netops creates an IAM role we can assume to create the Interface Endpoint (or we provide service name and they create it).
2) PH provides CIDR ranges for app subnets, NAT/egress policy, and whether private DNS should be enabled.
3) PH security sends back filled questionnaire and CMK preference.
4) Sales (elaine) to confirm POC dates and whether they want TGW or PrivateLink primary.

elaine_sales: I'll collect CIDRs and confirm POC start by EOD tomorrow. Few quick Qs from PH: do you require any outbound ports besides 443?

kevin_se: Typically only 443. Optional: 853 for DNS-over-TLS if they run DNS at app level, 123 for NTP to internal NTP (but normally apps use AWS NTP endpoints). If they block 443, nothing will work.

infra_bot: [automated] POC checklist created: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/poc-network-handoff (internal link) :white_check_mark:

sanjay_neteng: One blocker PH raised: their security baseline prevents cross-account ENI attachments unless approved. If that's the case, fallback is to use a shared services VPC with peering or TGW. We should surface this as a risk to the customer.

mike_se: Pricing note for procurement: PrivateLink traffic egress: we bill per GB and for Dedicated it can be included in committed capacity -- procurement to confirm whether they want committed monthly vs pay-as-you-go for the POC. I'll draft a one-pager.

elaine_sales: Great — I'll send the checklist + sec questionnaire and ask for CIDRs. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

kevin_se: Ping me on the ticket if they send firewall configs, I can review quickly.

tamara_ps: Will attach SOC2 link and a short diagram in the next message.

(END)
